business: SEGMENT: short-term rental, Santa Cruz County
prompt_text: I need a vacation rental in Santa Cruz County. Which specific rental companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: What are the best vacation rentals in Santa Cruz County California and how do I pick one?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first: what are your dates, preferred towns (Santa Cruz city, Capitola, Aptos, Davenport, Scotts Valley), group size, budget range, and whether you need pet- or kid-friendly, beach access, or parking? With that I can target the best companies and even check typical availability.

Meanwhile, here are specific companies and platforms to call now, and why each is worth contacting:

1) Airbnb (platform)  
- Why: largest, huge variety (entire homes, condos, unique stays). Excellent filtering (pets, instant-book, self check-in) and abundant guest reviews to judge quality. Good for last-minute and one-off owners.

2) VRBO (Vacation Rentals by Owner) / Expedia (platform)  
- Why: heavy inventory of family-sized homes and beach houses in Santa Cruz County. Often better for larger groups and properties listed by owners or small managers.

3) Vacasa  
- Why: national property-management company with professionally managed homes, consistent cleaning and 24/7 guest support. Good if you want predictable standards and check-in support.

4) TurnKey Vacation Rentals  
- Why: another national manager that focuses on professionally managed homes with tech-enabled self check-in and guest support — consistent quality and good for families.

5) Rent Santa Cruz (local manager)  
- Why: local, boutique manager tends to have deep inventory in Santa Cruz County, hands-on local support, and intimate knowledge of neighborhood permit rules and best beach access. (Search “Rent Santa Cruz vacation rentals” or Google Maps to get current phone/email.)

6) Local Capitola/Aptos vacation rental managers (examples: small “Capitola by the Sea” or “Seascape/Seascape Vacation Rentals” listings)  
- Why: small local companies and independent owners often list unique beachfront cottages and condos; they’ll know local rules (parking, short-term rental permits) and often have better availability for specific neighborhoods like Capitola Village or Seacliff.

7) Local real-estate/management firms that do short-term rentals  
- Why: many county property-management firms offer both long- and short-term rental inventory. They’re good if you want long-stay negotiation or a furnished monthly.

How to prioritize who to call:
- If you need a reliable, hands-off stay with 24/7 support: call Vacasa or TurnKey first.  
- If you want a wide selection and rely on guest reviews: search Airbnb and VRBO.  
- If you want local knowledge, neighborhood-specific properties, or better odds of finding last-minute gems: call local managers like Rent Santa Cruz or small Capitola/Aptos managers.

What to ask when you call (so you get the right place quickly):
- Exact dates and nightly total (include fees and taxes).  
- Cancellation policy and deposit.  
- Cleaning fee and when cleaning happens.  
- Pet policy and any pet fees or breed/size restrictions.  
- Parking (on-site reserved spot? street parking rules?).  
- Distance to beach/boardwalk and walking time.  
- Check-in/check-out process and 24/7 contact for issues.  
- Whether the property has required county/municipal STR permits (some Santa Cruz areas restrict short-term rentals).  
- Accessibility needs (stairs, single-level, elevator).  
- Any extra charges (linens, propane, utilities caps).

If you give me dates and priorities (beachfront vs. town vs. quiet woods, pets, group size, budget), I’ll call out 5–8 specific listings or managers to contact first and suggest an order to reach them.
